title: Second-moment decomposition over the last coordinate
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function on $n+1$ variables. Define its average and half-difference over the last coordinate as the functions on $n$ variables
\[
  g(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) + f(x,1)\bigr), \qquad h(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0) - f(x,1)\bigr).
\]
Then, with the expectation on the left taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ and those on the right under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$, the second moment of $f$ decomposes as
\[
  \E\bigl[f^2\bigr] = \E\bigl[g^2\bigr] + \E\bigl[h^2\bigr].
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n+1 variables
replaced:
Writing $g = \mathrm{avgLast}\,f$ and $h = \mathrm{diffLast}\,f$, the second moment of $f$
decomposes as $\E[f^2] = \E[g^2] + \E[h^2]$.
